rationale_summary: As an institutional implementing regulation, Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/454 relies on restrained legal recitals rather than broad policy rhetoric. Its dominant framing aligns with fundamental rights, explicitly mandating panel expertise in fundamental rights and equality alongside strict provider independence, impartiality, gender balance, public-interest commitment, and transparent public reporting. Consumer and public safety is a close secondary rationale, grounding the panel's core mandate to reinforce national market surveillance enforcement and transmit reasoned qualified alerts on general-purpose AI models to trigger Union supervisory intervention. Innovation enablement appears as a measured third rationale through repeated necessity and proportionality safeguards designed to protect providers' trade secrets and confidential business information during regulatory information demands.

evidence_spans.quote: multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary adequate and up-to-date scientific, technical, or sociotechnical expertise related to artificial intelligence, the impacts of artificial intelligence, or otherwise relevant to the effective enforcement of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, including expertise pertaining to applied sectors, fundamental rights and equality, as appropriate;

To avoid conflicts of interest in the performance of their tasks, experts of the scientific panel should be independent from any provider of AI systems or general-purpose AI models and should act independently, impartially and objectively. To ensure trust in the work of the scientific panel, experts should draw up declarations of interest and commitment to act in the public interest

To allow the reinforcement of national capacities necessary for the effective enforcement of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Member States’ market surveillance authorities should be able to call upon support from the scientific panel for their enforcement activities under that Regulation.

To ensure that the scientific panel can effectively issue qualified alerts to the AI Office pursuant to Article 90 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the conditions, procedures and detailed arrangements for the issuance of such qualified alerts should be set out.

The AI Office shall assess whether issuing a request for documentation or information to a provider of a general-purpose AI model is necessary and proportionate for the fulfilment of the tasks of the scientific panel, taking into account the need to protect trade secrets and confidential business information.
